# Module params come from -P, with typed defaults; a missing required param
# or a value of the wrong type is an error.
! bit show
stderr 'missing required param .stage. \(use -P stage=VALUE\)'
! exists show.txt

bit -P stage=prod show
grep '\Aprod-2 false\z' show.txt

bit -P stage=prod -P replicas=3 -P verbose=true show
stdout 'show ▶'
grep '\Aprod-3 true\z' show.txt

! bit -P stage=prod -P replicas=many show
stderr 'replicas: expected number, got string'

! bit -P stage=prod -P unknown=1 show
stderr 'unknown param: unknown'

bit -P stage=prod --info
stdout 'stage \(string\)'
stdout 'replicas \(number = 2\)'
stdout 'verbose \(bool = false\)'

# A parameterized target's defaults may use earlier parameters. Equal calls
# share one node, and different values make independent ones.
bit -P stage=prod both
stdout 'job\(name="a", out="a.out"\) ▶'
! stdout 'job\(name="a".*▶[\s\S]*job\(name="a".*▶'
stdout 'job\(name="b", out="b.out"\) ▶'
grep '\Aa\z' a.out
grep '\Ab\z' b.out
grep '\Aa\z' consumer.txt

bit -P stage=prod 'job' name=b
stdout 'job\(name="b", out="b.out"\) · no changes'

! bit -P stage=prod job
stderr 'invalid invocation of .job.: missing required argument .name.'

# A let that uses a missing param names the param to set, not the let.
cp let.bit BUILD.bit
! bit
stderr 'missing required param .p. \(use -P p=VALUE\)'
bit -P p=hi
stdout 't ✔'

-- let.bit --
param p : string
let l = p
t = exec { command = "echo #{l}" }
-- BUILD.bit --
param stage : string
param replicas : int = 2
param verbose = false

show = exec {
  command = "printf '%s-%s %s' #{stage} #{replicas} #{verbose} > show.txt"
  outputs = "show.txt"
}

job(name : string, out = "#{name}.out") = exec {
  command = "printf #{name} > #{out}"
  outputs = out
}

consumer = exec {
  command = "cat #{job(name = "a").path} > consumer.txt"
  outputs = "consumer.txt"
  depends_on = [job(name = "a")]
}

group both = [job(name = "a"), job(name = "b"), consumer]
